_readme: Screening thresholds, not engineering standards - tune them with the team. A road gets the demand tier only if it meets BOTH its average and its peak-hour motorcycles-diverted-per-hour minimums (all 168 day/hour slots; peak = hours 7-10 and 17-20), under the assumed diversion share.

low|compatible_assumed.text: Flyover not recommended: 2-wheeler demand is too low to justify it

any|unknown.text: Verdict withheld: surrounding-environment data not available

high|unknown.text: Provisional verdict: flyover looks justified on 2-wheeler demand

medium|unknown.text: Provisional verdict: flyover may be justified on 2-wheeler demand (second priority)

low|unknown.text: Provisional verdict: flyover not justified on 2-wheeler demand alone

site_labels.compatible_assumed: Environment considered feasible (straight road, metro in the median, 2 lanes each side, service road)

environment_note: The surrounding environment was considered feasible for this junction until site data is recorded. It cannot be guaranteed that it will remain the same once the site is surveyed.
data_notes: Demand figures are model estimates, not field counts.

The 6 corridor junctions (Electronic City, Kudlu Gate, HSR Layout, Bommanahalli, Hosa Road, Bommasandra) are derived from Silk Board's profile scaled by video counts; the other roads are area-level synthetic data.
Motorcycle share is a fixed published-survey mix (about 53%) applied to every road, not measured per junction.
inconclusive_note: This verdict is provisional. It cannot be concluded because surrounding-environment data is not available for this junction; it can be confirmed once the site data is recorded.
unknown_open_items: Road type, median and number of lanes
Service road and right-of-way / road width
